# permio_grant (Resource)

The roles and permissions granted to one principal (a user, service or group) directly on one resource URI.

This resource is **authoritative** for its (principal, resource) pair: it manages the complete set of roles and permissions granted directly to the principal on exactly that resource URI. On create and on every apply it grants what is missing and revokes anything else granted on the pair, including grants made outside Terraform. Destroying it revokes everything granted on the pair.

**Use exactly one `permio_grant` per principal and resource.** Two resources for the same pair would keep revoking each other's grants.

Grants are inherited: a grant on `/workspaces/acme` also applies to `/workspaces/acme/docs/1`, and a `_` segment matches any single segment (`/workspaces/_/billing`). Inherited grants on other URIs are separate pairs and are not touched by this resource.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "permio_permission" "read" {
  name = "document.read"
}

resource "permio_permission" "share" {
  name = "document.share"
}

resource "permio_role" "viewer" {
  name        = "Viewer"
  permissions = [permio_permission.read.name]
}

resource "permio_group" "support" {
  name = "support"
}

# Every member of the support group can read everything in workspace acme.
resource "permio_grant" "support_acme" {
  principal = permio_group.support.principal
  resource  = "/workspaces/acme"
  roles     = [permio_role.viewer.id]
}

# A user granted directly. A "_" segment matches any single segment,
# so this covers /workspaces/<any>/shared.
resource "permio_grant" "alice_shared" {
  principal   = "user_alice"
  resource    = "/workspaces/_/shared"
  roles       = [permio_role.viewer.id]
  permissions = [permio_permission.share.name]
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `principal` (String) Principal ID: a user or service ID from your system, or a group's principal (`group:<name>`, for example `permio_group.engineering.principal`). Changing it replaces the grant.
- `resource` (String) Resource URI, such as `/workspaces/acme/projects/42`. It must start with `/`, must not contain empty segments, a trailing `/`, whitespace, or any of `( ) [ ] { } * + ? | ^ $ \`, and is at most 2048 bytes. A `_` segment matches any single segment. Changing it replaces the grant.

### Optional

- `permissions` (Set of String) Names of the permissions to grant directly.
- `project` (String) Project the object belongs to. Defaults to the provider's `project`. Changing it replaces the object. API keys are scoped to one project, so this must be the key's project.
- `roles` (Set of String) IDs of the roles to grant (for example `permio_role.editor.id`), not role names.
- `timeouts` (Block, Optional) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) `<project>|<principal>|<resource>`.

<a id="nestedblock--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).
- `delete` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Setting a timeout for a Delete operation is only applicable if changes are saved into state before the destroy operation occurs.
- `read` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Read operations occur during any refresh or planning operation when refresh is enabled.
- `update` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Imported by "<project>|<principal>|<resource URI>", or "<principal>|<resource URI>" for the provider's project.
# ("|" is used because principals and resource URIs can contain "/"; resource URIs cannot contain "|".)
terraform import permio_grant.support_acme "default|group:support|/workspaces/acme"
```
